clue.text: Pop round, run over greater distance

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Dad goes out for a jog and covers more ground than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative adverb means at a more distant point, a greater way off.

clue.text: Temporarily abroad, lead is missing from show

parts.note: forth means out, abroad, away from home

indicators.note: says the first letter of the word for show is dropped

parts.note: to represent is to show or depict

explanation.surface: Away for now, the star is absent from the production.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for now, for the time being.

clue.text: Book 8

definitions.meaning: to book is to secure in advance
the entry at 8 across, meaning control or holding back

explanation.walkthrough: The bare number points to the answer at 8 across, whose meaning is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve means to book a seat, and also self-control or reticence.

clue.text: Houdini in trouble

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Houdini's first name was this, and it also means to harass or pester.

clue.text: Cover again checks on river

parts.note: reins are checks or restraints
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Insurance is renewed after controls are placed on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure once more is to provide a fresh insurance cover.

clue.text: Solicitor has something to eat in pub

indicators.note: in places the snack inside the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one
an egg is something to eat

explanation.surface: A lawyer orders a bite at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it is simply one who solicits, asking for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone begging solicits alms from passers-by, so a solicitor in the literal sense.

clue.text: Predict fish will be found in shop

parts.note: to bet that something will happen is to predict it
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A forecast that fish will be on sale in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is not a store but the slang verb to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is slang for informing on them, giving them away.

clue.text: Examination of some quango in government

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An inspection of a quasi-official body within the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough inspection or check of something is this informal phrase.

clue.text: Flier advertising very innovative academy that only recently opened

indicators.note: opened points to the letters that begin each of the words

parts.words: advertising very innovative academy that only recently

explanation.surface: A leaflet promotes a newly founded academy with a fresh approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a leaflet, but it means a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aircraft is one who flies it.

clue.text: Control number of carriages allowed in halt

indicators.note: allowed in says the carriages are let inside the stop

parts.note: a rest is a halt or pause
a train is a number of carriages coupled together

explanation.surface: Rail authorities limit how many carriages may stand at a stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Control and holding back are synonyms for self-discipline.

clue.text: Tongue I savour — but not the Spanish version

indicators.note: but not says letters are taken away from the word for savour

parts.note: to relish something is to savour it
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A gourmet enjoys a dish of tongue, except when it is prepared the Spanish way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like food on a menu, and 'Spanish version' like a recipe, but the tongue is a language and the version is only a translation of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and Irish is the Gaelic language of Ireland.

clue.text: Creature randomly chooses her bra

indicators.note: randomly says the letters are mixed in no particular order

explanation.surface: A woman picks a bra at random.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine arthropod with a hard domed shell is a kind of creature.

clue.text: Courageous flag-captain

definitions.meaning: brave, bold, tough in the face of danger
Thomas Masterman ... was Nelson's flag-captain on HMS Victory at Trafalgar

explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's dying words were famously addressed to Captain Hardy at the Battle of Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy means bold and robust, and Hardy was the captain of Nelson's flagship.

clue.text: Real thugs can bring this about

definitions.text: Real thugs can bring this about

indicators.note: bring about suggests turning the letters round into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Genuine villains are capable of causing a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram of REAL THUGS and a description of what such people might cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Real thugs can bring about killing on a large scale, a massacre.

clue.text: Graph transferred from chapter I

indicators.note: transferred says the letters are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diagram has been lifted from the opening chapter of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular chart divided into slices is a kind of graph.

clue.text: With the cards dealt to them, do bridge players fit together easily?

definitions.text: With the cards dealt to them, do bridge players fit together easily?

parts.words: With the cards dealt to them, do bridge players fit together easily?
parts.note: playing cards laid face down on the table, and the idiom for winning without effort

explanation.surface: A question about whether card players get along once dealt their cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means easily, and also describes cards held by players placed downward.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning without difficulty, effortlessly, as in winning by a wide margin.

clue.text: Opposed to state's economics initially

parts.note: to aver is to state, so the clue's possessive gives avers

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word economics

explanation.surface: Someone is hostile to the government's economic policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means disliking or being against it.

clue.text: Record I had turned up in church — I'm seen everywhere

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I had contracts to I'd

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up reads the letters from bottom to top
in places the I'm inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
I'm without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A singer finds their record has turned up in church; they're everywhere now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down entry, where the church-and-I'm piece is read from the bottom upwards; the definition is adjectival, describing anything widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread throughout a population, like a disease, is described this way.

clue.text: Closure imminent when pressure's dropped

indicators.note: dropped says the letter for pressure is removed

parts.note: pending means about to happen, imminent
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A shutdown looms once the pressure falls, as at a failing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is a close or conclusion, the point of finishing.

clue.text: Grieved horribly, becoming separate

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A couple, deeply upset, part ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To diverge is to go separate ways, to branch off.

clue.text: Draw near a very quiet fish

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler creeps up quietly on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To come close to something is to move towards it.

clue.text: 101-letter question — answer comes up as "connected with water"

indicators.note: in a down entry, comes up says the letters are read from bottom upwards

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
tau is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A quiz asks question 101 and the answer reveals something about water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' reverses all four pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things living in or relating to water.

clue.text: Startled Turkish commander's on time

parts.note: an agha is a Turkish military commander

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer is surprised to be punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aghast is being shocked or filled with horror.

clue.text: Imagined wrong is avenged

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A wronged person who has taken revenge pictures how it went.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in the mind is to imagine or foresee it.

clue.text: Dickens, with reason, died only once

indicators.note: only once says the letter for died should appear a single time, so one copy is removed

parts.note: to deduce is to reason
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A remark about the novelist, who logically could die only once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' is not the novelist but the mild oath, as in 'what the dickens?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dickens and the deuce are interchangeable mild oaths meaning the devil.

clue.text: Object reserved but not finally suitable

indicators.note: but not says a letter is removed from the word for reserved

parts.note: demure means reserved or modest

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of suitable

explanation.surface: A shy item that, in the end, is not appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb, to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise objections or show reluctance.

clue.text: To a T? Just approximately this is unfinished

parts.note: the letter T as written
or so means just about, approximately

explanation.surface: A question of exactness answered with a shrug about something incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: A torso in art is a sculpted trunk with no head or limbs, an unfinished figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted trunk lacking head and limbs looks like an incomplete statue.

clue.text: Old university has to adapt, providing accommodation for people with higher degrees

indicators.note: providing accommodation for says one word houses the others inside

parts.note: to alter is to adapt
MA, Master of Arts, is a higher degree holder
a second MA, since the clue's people are plural

explanation.surface: An old college must change to house postgraduates.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduates call the university they attended their old institution by this Latin phrase.

clue.text: Fruit tart I rejected, and fish sent back

indicators.note: rejected says the letter I is thrown out

parts.note: a pie is a tart

indicators.note: sent back says the fish is written backwards

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A diner turns down a fruit tart and returns the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the groundnut is a fruit, a legume pod with seeds.

clue.text: Bit of maize revealed by my new horse

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise like my!
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A newly bought horse turns out to be eating corn.
explanation.definitionFit: The central woody core of an ear of maize is part of the plant.
